solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Location at which many are canvassed?

definitions.text: Location at which many are canvassed?

parts.words: Location at which many are canvassed?
parts.note: canvassed suggests being polled by an election campaigner, but here it means sheltered under canvas, as in a field full of tents

explanation.surface: A question about where a big opinion poll takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvassed' reads as political doorstepping; the second sense is being put under canvas, which is what happens to holidaymakers in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a field where campers pitch tents, each sleeping under canvas.

clue.text: Bird with left foot hidden in weed

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster

indicators.note: hidden says the letters for foot are tucked away out of sight, so they drop from the word left

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A bird with one foot tucked out of sight, standing among the weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it means the abbreviation for foot is taken out of sight. 'In' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Corncockle, or cockle, is a weed of cornfields with purple flowers.

clue.text: An illusion? I am churning over with anger

indicators.note: turning over means the short form of I am is flipped end to end

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, giving IM
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their churning fury is just imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churning over' suggests an anagram, but it is a turnover: the contraction is flipped end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert that is not there.

clue.text: After second drink I have to be frolicsome

indicators.note: after says the drink and I have follow the letter for second

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
I have contracts to I've, giving IVE

explanation.surface: A drinker says a second glass makes them feel playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful or frisky, a near synonym of frolicsome.

clue.text: Bird regularly spotted in the fall

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the words the fall, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a bird often seen in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small dabbling duck.

clue.text: Duke will back the country, it's said

indicators.note: back here means support from behind, so the letter for Duke goes after the country

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A rumour that a duke will support his nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated is a past participle synonym of said, as in a declared or expressed view.

clue.text: Grating in street held up dogs

indicators.note: in places the grating inside the turned-round letters
in a down clue held up means read from the bottom upwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: a rack is a framework of bars, like a grating

explanation.surface: Dogs are held up by a drain grating in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' reads upwards, so the street abbreviation turns round; 'in' sets the grating inside it. 'Dogs' looks like animals but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, which is to track them.

clue.text: Pay attention when there's ghastly death — eek!

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something horribly disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, fodder
taken as written, fodder

explanation.surface: A scream of eek at a horrible death is a warning to be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed is to pay attention or be careful, an idiom.

clue.text: State English rule in bold act

indicators.note: in puts English and rule inside the bold act

parts.note: a dare is a daring act, done on a challenge
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: An English law made in a brave deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a US state, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: NCO — gosh, quietly spoken!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A soldier mutters a quiet exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer, abbreviated NCO.

clue.text: Animal sailor attached to a line

parts.note: jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is tied to a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild dog of Africa and Asia, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Break item possibly?

parts.note: item possibly suggests a rearrangement of the word item; the word time with out, an anagram signal, would lead back to it

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, TIME with OUT as an anagram signal, and it produces ITEM, which 'possibly' marks as one result.
explanation.definitionFit: A time-out is a short break or pause, as in sport.

clue.text: Ambassador joining the French people at match

parts.note: le is French for the
the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match

explanation.surface: A French diplomat joins the crowd at a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is the attendance at a sports event, a common British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy or papal ambassador.

clue.text: Show contempt for dramatist's worthless article

parts.note: to kick at something is to spurn it, showing contempt
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a playwright's trashy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickshaw is a trinket or trifle, a worthless thing; the word comes from French quelque chose.

clue.text: Hurt in game and is put into bed

indicators.note: put into places the game and is inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written
RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: An injured player is tucked into bed after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is Rugby Union, conventionally RU; 'put into' places it with 'is' inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruised means injured or hurt, physically or emotionally.

clue.text: Look after maiden perhaps going to 24?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, an example of an over
24 down is a cathedral city, which is the seat of a bishop's diocese, called a see

explanation.surface: A young woman heads off to a city to take care of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over of six balls in which no runs are scored. The cross-reference 24 is a cathedral city, and every cathedral city is a see.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, which is to look after something.

clue.text: Try in this place to get listened to

indicators.note: listened to signals that the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to get a hearing here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a judge tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear a case in court is to try it, the legal sense.

clue.text: Bird hard for country person to bag

indicators.note: to bag is to hold inside, so the country person contains the letter for hard

parts.note: a peasant is a rural worker
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A game bird is tough for a farmer to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: Square meal not half awkward in tents

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, fodder

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word meal, its first two letters, is kept

explanation.surface: A hearty dinner is clumsily served in tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square meal' looks like one idea; SQUARE is whole fodder and 'not half' keeps ME from MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquees are large tents used for parties and shows.

clue.text: Danger when padre dances with joy

indicators.note: dances suggests letters moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, fodder
taken as written, fodder

explanation.surface: A risky moment as a chaplain dances for joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is peril or danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The man will, it's said, get well again

indicators.note: it's said signals that the contraction is spoken, giving a similar sounding word

parts.note: the man will contracts to he'll

explanation.surface: A rumour that a man will recover his health.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to recover, getting well after an injury or illness.

clue.text: Very small society's account of what happened at meeting

definitions.text: account of what happened at meeting

parts.note: minute means very small
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A tiny club keeps a record of its gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUTE is pronounced my-NEWT here, but the plural noun is said MIN-its.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the official written record of a meeting.

clue.text: Starts eating at home, superior lodgings

indicators.note: superior means placed above, so in this down entry the lodgings come above at home

parts.note: digs is British slang for rented lodgings
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone tucks in at home, in smart rented rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGS is British slang for rented rooms; 'superior' puts it above IN in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an idiom for starting to eat heartily.

clue.text: Notice a soldier with love for slow music

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
GI is an American soldier
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A soldier posts a lonely hearts notice about slow songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical direction meaning slowly, also a piece played that way.

clue.text: Old saint not keeping quiet in cathedral city

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: not keeping means the letter for quiet is dropped from the saint's name

parts.note: Saint Peter, the apostle
p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: An ancient saint makes noise in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not keeping quiet' reads as a noisy saint, but 'not keeping' drops the musical letter for quiet from the apostle's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter, in Devon, is an English city with a cathedral.

clue.text: Got hold of many sheets of paper to be put into a record

indicators.note: put into places the sheets inside a and the record

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record
a quire is 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Stacks of paper are filed into an archive.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE goes between A-C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired means obtained, which is getting hold of something.

clue.text: Cluster of flowers, number outside bedsit?

indicators.note: outside means the number goes around the bedsit

parts.note: six is a number
a pad is a slang term for a small flat such as a bedsit

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers sits beside the house number of a small flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat; PAD is slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadix is a fleshy spike of tiny flowers, as in arum lilies.

clue.text: Frame of ship in port

definitions.meaning: the main body of a vessel
a seaport city in Yorkshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: The hull is a ship's body, and Hull is an English port on the Humber estuary.

clue.text: A leg-puller is relaxed

parts.note: a tease is a joker who pulls your leg

explanation.surface: A prankster is easygoing.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease means relaxed and comfortable, an idiom.

clue.text: Utter a word of dismissal, just

parts.note: out is what an umpire says to dismiss a batsman, or what someone says to send a person away
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: Saying a single fair word to dismiss someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective: complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and outright both mean complete or total, as in an outright lie.

clue.text: Tea's in — this herbal infusion's out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, fodder

explanation.surface: Ordinary tea is popular, but this herbal drink is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'out' look like a fashion contrast; 'out' is the anagram signal for TEASIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, made by infusing leaves or flowers.

clue.text: One viewing a sequence of acts?

definitions.text: One viewing a sequence of acts?

parts.words: One viewing a sequence of acts?
parts.note: acts suggests deeds in general, but read as theatre it is the acts of a drama, watched by an audience member

explanation.surface: A question about someone watching a series of deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre audience member watches a play, which is made up of acts.
